answers:
The IBM Watson Text-to-Speech service supports various SSML elements and attributes to control text synthesis. If you need specific information about the level of support for all SSML elements, please refer to the SSML elements page.
Additionally, the service supports enhanced neural and expressive neural voices  with features like modifying speaking rate, modifying speaking pitch, using speaking styles, emphasizing interjections, and emphasizing words.

history.content: SSML stands for Speech Synthesis Markup Language. It is an XML-based markup language used to annotate text for speech synthesis applications. It provides a standard way for developers to control various aspects of the synthesis process, including pronunciation, volume, pitch, speed, and other attributes. It operates by augmenting the plain text that is passed to a synthesizer with a predefined set of elements, or tags. Additionally, it is used in the IBM Watson Text to Speech service as well.

An SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) element is any content enclosed by an opening tag and its corresponding closing tag. For example, an element can include a mix of other elements and text. Furthermore, elements can have required attributes or may optionally accept attributes set to specific values.

Yes, there is IBM Watson Text-to-Speech service support for SSML elements and attributes for controlling text synthesis. Additionally, there is a WebSocket interface service now that supports the use of the SSML element as well.

SSML elements 

With the IBM Watson® Text to Speech service, you can use most Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) elements and attributes to control the synthesis of your text.



 Supported elements and attributes 

Table 1 summarizes the service's support for SSML elements and attributes:



* Full means that the service fully supports the element or attribute with its HTTP and WebSocket interfaces.
* Partial means that the service's support for the element or attribute is limited in one of the following ways:



* The service supports only some aspects of the element or attribute.
* The service supports the element or attribute with only some of its voices.
* The service supports the element or attribute with only one of its interfaces, HTTP or WebSocket.



* None means that the service does not support the element or attribute.

SSML elements 

With the IBM Watson® Text to Speech service, you can use most Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) elements and attributes to control the synthesis of your text.

Supported elements and attributes 

Table 1 summarizes the service's support for SSML elements and attributes:



* Full means that the service fully supports the element or attribute with its HTTP and WebSocket interfaces.

SSML validation 

The service validates all SSML elements that you submit in any content, either as input text for synthesis or as the definition of a word's translation for customization. The service cannot determine ahead of time whether text submitted for synthesis contains SSML elements. Therefore, it performs the same validation for all input text, regardless of whether it contains SSML.
